speaker: Doctor
text: That sounds like sciatica. Can you tell me if the pain started after a specific injury or if it came on while you were sleeping? Also, on a scale of 1 to 10, how severe is the pain?

speaker: Patient
text: 26-year-old woman. The patient reports exercising in the gym several hours ago when she suddenly felt a sharp pain in her lower back. She describes the pain as radiating down the side of her leg and into her foot.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Lumbar Disc Herniation (likely L4-L5 or L5-S1).

To confirm this and rule out cauda equina syndrome, I need to know if you have any loss of bowel or bladder control, or numbness in the saddle area. Additionally, please tell me if you have weakness in lifting your foot (foot drop) or difficulty standing on your toes.
